exposure: Mode of birth (elective cesarean section vs. other)
outcome: Umbilical cord blood hematocrit (Hct) levels at birth
Capillary heel Hct levels at 48 hours
cohort: The study included 66 infants of diabetic mothers (IDM) and a 1:2 matched control group.
finding: Infants of diabetic mothers (IDM) presented with significantly lower cord blood Hct levels and an estimated extra circulating fluid loss of 2-3% compared to controls, indicating an excess of circulating fluids during the transition from fetal to neonatal life.
mod_finding: The significantly lower cord blood Hct levels in infants of diabetic mothers were mainly observed if delivered by elective cesarean section.
